title: Missing-prime keys and routes: checking the score
question: Do the pinned missing-prime anchor trigger and the resulting source score pass known-text and shuffled-text controls before applying them to unsolved pages?
reader_question: Can the missing-prime and grid-key score distinguish a reading from shuffled text?
summary: A source program launches two numeric keys and route searches after three consecutive missing-prime word sums. Its unigram score passes every one of 199 shuffled controls for both keys on a known reading, and route order cannot change that score.
finding: The synthetic three-word anchor triggered once and a broken sequence did not. Both pinned keys and six routes recovered a planted known reading. Yet all 199 shuffled controls for each key exceeded the source score bar after trying 29 Atbash shifts; all 199 route shuffles also passed, and any route permutation leaves this unigram score unchanged. No unsolved-page anchor counts or decodes were run.
limitations: One 157-rune known reading was used and it contributed to the source solved-page frequency target; these are in-sample operator controls, not a general power estimate. The original score bars are weak on this fixture, but the key and route hypotheses are not excluded. The source key spelling differs from its own page transcription at five already documented cells; source/site punctuation changes word boundaries on three LP2 pages.
next_steps: Freeze an order-sensitive English screen and matched full-search controls, then separately report source-transcription anchor counts before running any candidate key or route search on unsolved pages.

scope.representation: Pinned source secrets.cpp 256-pair stream and 180 missing primes; one 157-rune known direct reading from source Page 5. Synthetic three-word anchor and 199 shuffled conditional score controls; no unsolved LP2 target search.
scope.procedure: Verify source constants and five grid case differences; test three-word trigger, invert two key streams and six source route positions on a known reading; scan all 29 source Atbash shifts on 199 seeded shuffles for each key and use unigram invariance for routes.
scope.parameters: Missing-prime sums 73,79,83; keys of lengths 256 and 180; source strict score thresholds >0.91 (keys) and >0.90 (routes); route widths 3 and 7; 199 deterministic controls seeded 3301..3499.
scope.exclusions: No claim that an unsolved page contains an anchor, that either key/route decodes LP2, that other passages have the same control behavior, or that source letter-case ambiguities are resolved.

review.reviewer: Independent checker recalculates 398 key-control maxima, six route plants and invariant route score; source C++ fixture confirms original tokenizer, anchor and key transforms

reproduction.environment: Python 3 standard library; all ordinary check inputs are included. Optional source-controls.cpp needs a pinned upstream C++ checkout and C++20 compiler.

visuals.caption: Each source key exceeded its score threshold on all 199 shuffled controls; changing route order cannot change unigram fitness.

sources.label: Pinned original search and score rules

reader_finding: The source’s score accepted all 199 shuffled controls for each key. Rearranging the runes cannot change this score, so it cannot select a route. A high score here does not establish a readable message.
reader_limit: This checks the scoring rule on one known passage. It does not test the keys on unsolved pages or rule out the proposed keys and routes.
